name: royal banner pole, 3/4 top-down: square stone foot (top face seen from above, front face), wooden pole with iron bands, gold spear-tip finial, crossbar with a hanging blue banner (gold border, gold crown over a gold eight-point star, swallowtail)
label: beodeul_city/capital/capital_banner_pole

surfaces.part: hanging blue banner with crown and star

answer.evidence: The stone foot (rows 36-46, width 12) is the only solid volume. Rows 36-41 are a light top face (L~208-222), followed by a darker edge line at row 42 and an eave shadow at row 43. Rows 42-46 are its front face (5 rows). The pole is thin and the banner is a hanging cloth, which I count as decor like a flag. The crossbar is a thin 2-row strip with a lighter row 4 above a dark row 5, so I counted it as having a top.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a thin, tall prop, so I judged it by eye against the thin references (lamp-crook, bench) as well as the larger props. It has 13 visible tones per tile, 0% near-flat coverage and only 18% neutral dark edge pixels, so its outlines lean toward the neighbouring material (dark blue beside the banner, brown beside the pole) and are not a uniform black line. That is richer than the lamp-crook (14 raw colours, 100% neutral outline) and the bench (44% neutral). The candidate has 30 distinct colours in total, against 14 for each of those two. The banner has a gold border, crown and star emblem, and the swallowtail is readable. The stone foot shows a top face and a front face with some shading, the pole has iron bands, and there is a finial. Each material shows about 3-4 steps, a little below Beodeul's 5-6 on the large props, and the texture is modest rather than rich. It is still not a flat sticker, and a careful artist would accept it next to the thin references without it looking thinner or flatter.

surfaces.part: hanging banner with crown and star

answer.evidence: The main body is the square stone foot (width 12, rows 36-46). Rows 36-41 are a light top face seen from above, with a socket for the pole at rows 38-39. A front-edge line at row 42 (L=169) is followed by a dark shadow row at 43 (L=90). The front face is rows 42-46, about 5 rows, with a panel line. The pole (rows 29-35, width 2) and the crossbar (rows 4-5) are thin structural parts. The banner hangs vertically and is decor, like a flag on a pole. No isometric side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a thin, sparse prop, so I judged it mostly by eye and by the measured facts. It has 13 visible tones per 16x16 tile, which is above the hedge (9) and close to the cheese stall (17) and roofed well (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so the blue banner is not a flat fill. It has 30 distinct colours in total, against 14 for the lamp and bench, the closest thin references. Only 18% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outlines lean toward a tint (dark blue beside the banner, dark brown beside the pole) rather than a black sticker line. The banner cloth, pole and stone foot each show about 3-4 lightness steps. That is slightly shallower than Beodeul's 5-6 per material, but it is comparable to the other thin references and not flat. The gold border, crown and star add distinct detail, and the stone foot has separate top and front faces. A careful artist would accept it next to the lamp and stall without it looking thinner or more sticker-like.

surfaces.part: hanging banner with crown and star

answer.evidence: The main body is the stone foot, rows 36-46, 12 px wide. Rows 36-41 are a light top face (L about 208-222), 6 rows deep. A lighter-to-darker transition at rows 42-43 (L 169, then 90) marks the front-edge line and eave shadow. Below it the front face of rows 42-46 shows a brick pattern. The pole, the 2-row crossbar and the hanging banner are thin vertical elements and are not major volumes needing a top. The banner is cloth hanging from the crossbar and is treated as decor. The foot matches the green reference pattern of a top surface, an edge line and a front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a thin prop about one tile wide, so I judged it mostly by eye against the lamp-crook and bench, with the measured facts as support. It carries 13 visible tones per full tile. That is above the hedge (9) and below the stall (17) and well (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so it has no large flat fills. Only 18% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so the outlines lean toward the neighbouring material (dark blue beside the banner, dark brown beside the pole) rather than a black sticker line. The stone foot shows a lit top face and a darker front face, the pole has iron bands, and the banner has a gold border with a crown and star emblem. This is clearly richer than the plain lamp-crook reference. Each material ramp is about 3-4 steps against the references' 5-6, and the texture grain is light, so I rate density slightly lower than the references rather than equal. That is acceptable for a thin prop and it does not look like a sticker next to them.

surfaces.part: wooden pole with iron bands and gold finial

answer.evidence: The only volumetric main body is the square stone foot at rows 36-46 (width 12). Rows 36-40 form a light top face about 5 rows tall (L≈222 at x=4 and L≈208 at x=11). Row 41 is a slightly darker front-edge line (L≈197), and rows 42-46 are the front face with darker block detail, about 5 rows. The pole is a thin 2px vertical shaft and the banner is flat hanging cloth, so neither needs a top surface. The crossbar at rows 4-5 is a thin beam with a lighter upper row and a dark lower row that works as a shadow, so it is acceptable.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 13 visible tones per 16x16 tile, between the hedge (9) and the stall (17) and well (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills. Only 18% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so the outlines lean toward the material tone (dark blue beside the banner, dark brown beside the pole, grey-blue beside the stone) rather than a sticker-style black line. The banner has a gold border, a crown and star emblem, and a blue field with at least 3 steps. The stone foot shows a top face and a front face with some speckle. The wooden pole with iron bands is thin and has fewer ramp steps, about 3-4, so the whole piece sits slightly below the richest references (well, stall) in shading depth. Next to the bench, lamp and hedge it matches or exceeds their density and does not look thinner or flatter, so it is acceptable.
